comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The mobile Google SERP leaves a broken AI Overview panel (only the sparkle icon and the "Не удалось сгенерировать обзор…" error) because the filter blocks its async/folsrch request; an unfiltered control renders the real overview. Adding google.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠data-async-type="folsrch"]⁠ to the existing "! Google Search - AI Overview" block in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/annoyances.txt verified clean (panel hidden, page intact), covering the page the older :⁠has() wrapper rule at line 354 no longer hides. ## Rule `google.com##div[data-async-type="folsrch"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale No closing rule in the run instruction applies:⁠ this is not a paywall, not a self-promotion banner, not an anti-adblock wall and not a scam page — it is an empty/broken leftover of a module the filter already blocks on purpose. It is a missed leftover on a fully reachable page, so it gets a rule; the AdGuard Other Annoyances purpose (irritating in-page elements) covers the broken AI Overview shell, and google.com has ample traffic. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/annoyances.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c8892e39d7c9aab33d8841e45827df5c4a7dc7ce/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/annoyances.txt) Under the heading `! SECTION: Other annoyances - Uncategorized`, before [line 357](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c8892e39d7c9aab33d8841e45827df5c4a7dc7ce/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/annoyances.txt#L357). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45518836641 Automated analysis against filters at `c8892e3`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"79fa9835e8fbb3c5146a12b49833c0b99b10124fdc60c1a956331a9540940610"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported in-player Hulu ad could not be reproduced:⁠ the reported watch URL 301-redirects to the unsigned-in Castle series page, and complete full-page vision of that page (reporterSymptomPresence absent, 0 instances) shows no player, ad, placeholder or gap. The repository's existing "Hulu video ads" rules (BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt 22787-22794, replace.txt line 10) were active, so no new rule is warranted; a maintainer with a Hulu subscription should verify the player case before closing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The AdguardFilters run instruction states no rule that closes this report:⁠ it is an ads report (T:⁠ Ads, P1:⁠ Critical) and none of the instruction's closing categories (paywall, unreachable anti-adblock detector without a captured detector script, scam page) is established by the evidence. Policy lookup (KnowledgeBase filter-policy.md + CONTRIBUTING.md) returned no criterion that refuses an ad-blocking rule for a streaming player, so rule generation is allowed and the decision rests on reproduction.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"608d5e137406474acfc77c066c18d23eadb352f2672c99b230ad6ef797695c48"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Live A/B/C experiments show filtering does break bypass.city's AceCaptcha (rings draw with no rules applied, blank challenge body with the reporter's baseline), and AdGuard CLI's shared Base filter XHR/denyallow rule blocks hc.acecaptcha.com, but a site-scoped allowlist exception - and even unfiltering the captcha's frames - left the challenge blank while the page showed its own "a content blocker may be stopping it" notice. No rule could be validated, so the report needs a maintainer's judgement on the site's ad/blocker gate.

## Still visible after the rule

- Centered AceCaptcha panel near top-middle of page, challenge body below the header/instruction line (approx. x=780–1135, y=218–465) — AceCaptcha verification panel heading and instruction text render, but the challenge body beneath is a completely empty dark rectangle with no ring targets, challenge graphics, or loading indicator — the interactive CAPTCHA content is missing.
- Centered AceCaptcha panel near top-middle of page, challenge body below the header/instruction line (approx. x=788–1145, y=218–465) — Same AceCaptcha panel with heading and instruction rendered while the challenge area stays a blank dark rectangle; no ring targets or challenge content are drawn, so verification cannot be completed.
- Centered AceCaptcha panel near top-middle of page, challenge body below the header/instruction line (approx. x=780–1135, y=221–466) — AceCaptcha panel again shows only its header and instruction with an empty dark challenge body; the ring-target challenge is absent, matching the reporter's missing-CAPTCHA-content symptom.
- AceCaptcha panel centered in the upper-middle of the page, roughly x=775-1135, y=210-465 within the tile; blank challenge area below the heading and instruction lines — The AceCaptcha widget's header ('Hold the ring with a gap', 'Follow it if it moves. Let go when it's full.', 'AceCaptcha' label) renders, but the region where the ring/hold challenge should be drawn is a large empty dark rectangle with no ring targets, ring outline, cursor target, or any CAPTCHA content at all. The interactive challenge content is missing, so the verification cannot be performed.
- Center of viewport:⁠ AceCaptcha panel headed 'Hold the ring with a gap' (approx. x=780–1142, y=210–470) — The AceCaptcha panel heading, instruction text, and 'AceCaptcha' label render, but the challenge area below is a blank dark rectangle with no ring targets or other interactive CAPTCHA content. This matches the reporter-described missing CAPTCHA content.

## Missing information

- No way to isolate the breaking filter/scriptlet in the adguard_cli proxy environment: In the locked adguard_cli environment, launch_browser accepts extension "none" only and refuses settings ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠""), so the documented list-halving / settings.slice isolation procedure cannot be run at all, and there is no unfiltered control session to diff against other than apply_rule phase A. Additionally, get_applied_rules explicitly does not report $csp, $permissions, $removeparam, $removeheader, $replace or extended-CSS (#⁠?#⁠) actions, and reports element hiding only for the frames the reader can address; the captcha widget renders inside cross-origin hc.acecaptcha.com frames that evaluate_js and the structure probe cannot read. The full per-phase console log and the captcha frame's DOM were therefore unavailable, so the specific rule that stops the AceCaptcha challenge from drawing on bypass.city could not be named.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"22ad6a7937f6c822498695786d2e1d79244634f86374f0c4f8e50a19aedcffb8"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's breakage reproduces:⁠ the mine player is replaced by the site's own video.js error ("No available working or supported playlists" / "your internet provider censor us"), while the unfiltered page plays the film once the site's pre-init gate is dismissed. Two Base-filter rules together cause it — the trusted-replace-xhr-response "Timeout:⁠0" scriptlet (line 780) makes the site skip its pre-init gate, and the .player-pre-init-ads CSS hide (line 779) makes that gate's close control unusable; each scoped exception was validated and rejected because the film still would not play, so the two lines need changing together.

## Still visible after the rule

- Main content under 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone 2001', around the 'REPORT AN ISSUE' bar and above the TRAILER / DOWNLOAD / WATCH LATER / FAVOURITES button row — The movie playback area is absent. No video player, video frame, controls, countdown overlay, or other playback content appears in the region where the film should play; the page moves directly into the report-issue bar and action buttons.
- Main movie playback region, between the 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone 2001' heading and the TRAILER/DOWNLOAD/WATCH LATER/FAVOURITES buttons — No video player, video frame, playback controls, error message, or placeholder block is visible; the movie playback area is missing, leaving only the title, REPORT AN ISSUE bar, and action buttons.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45525640441

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Indeterminate — The reported false positive does not reproduce with the AdGuard filter baseline:⁠ download.zspace.cn loads cleanly through the locked filtering proxy (56 requests, 0 blocked, no console errors) and the annotated "极空间 Skill" section renders in full — heading, zspace-nas-agent-toolkit package card with size/version/platform metadata and both install buttons — matching the reporter's "AdGuard disabled" screenshot. The reporter's own setup also runs third-party catalogs (EasyList China, EasyPrivacy, etc.) that have no executable baseline in this environment, so no filter rule behind the loss of content could be named and no evidence-backed exception can be proposed.

The reported breakage (the content of download.zspace.cn's #⁠skill section missing) is absent with every AdGuard list the reporter uses, so the culprit rule — if it is a filter rule at all — can only be in one of these unavailable catalogs, which this run cannot execute or inspect.

issue.title: Remove Adguard rules for tempo.com, which has a new owner and thus different content

labels.name: Stale
labels.description: The issue was not processed on time and was bumped to the top of the list

issue.body: ### Prerequisites - [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml); - [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue; - [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date; - [x] Browser version is up-to-date; - [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue. ### What product do you use? Other ad blocker ### AdGuard version Helium built-in ad blocker ### What type of problem have you encountered? Website or app doesn't work properly ### Which browser(s) do you use? other (specify in comment below) ### Which device do you use? Desktop ### Where is the problem encountered? https://tempo.com/blog/introducing-mercator/ ### Ad Blocking AdGuard Base filter ### Privacy _No response_ ### Social Widgets _No response_ ### Annoyances AdGuard Cookie Notices filter ### Security _No response_ ### Other _No response_ ### DNS filters _No response_ ### Language-specific _No response_ ### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled? _No response_ ### Add your comment and screenshots 1. **tempo.com has changed owners. The Meteored rules for it now break the site and should drop `tempo.com`.** tempo.com used to be Meteored's Italian weather site. Since Nov 17, 2026 it is the website of Tempo, a payments company, and has no Meteored code. The Meteored rules still apply to it, and one of them breaks the layout. **Breaking rule** (AdGuard Cookie Notices filter): ``` yourweather.co.uk,tempo.com,daswetter.com#$#body { position: absolute !important; } ``` This rule shrinks `` to its content width (1320px in a 1989px window). The fixed header stays centred on the full window, the article is centred on only the left part, and the area to the right of the body is never painted, so it shows as a black block. Turning the blocker off fixes it. Safari, which doesn't have the rule, shows the page correctly. Applying the rule in plain Chromium reproduces the same broken layout. Browser: Helium (Chromium-based) on macOS, with its built-in ad blocker and the AdGuard lists above. **Please remove `tempo.com` from these rules.** They all target Meteored markup. The other domains stay as they are. | File | Line | Rule | |---|---|---| | AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt | [10892](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L10892) | `yourweather.co.uk,tempo.com,daswetter.com#$##gpdr { display: none !important; }` | | AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt | [10893](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L10893) | `yourweather.co.uk,tempo.com,daswetter.com#$#body { position: absolute !important; }` (breaks layout) | | AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt | [1590](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt#L1590) | `yourweather.co.uk,theweather.net,tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*##.descarga-app` | | AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt | [5311](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt#L5311) | `tiempo.com,meteored.*,theweather.net,yourweather.co.uk,tempo.pt,tempo.com##.modulo-suscripcion` | | MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt | [1712](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt#L1712) | `yourweather.co.uk,theweather.net,tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*#$#.pie-pagina { margin-bottom: 0 !important; }` | | SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt | [6294](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L6294) | `yourweather.co.uk,theweather.net,meteored.*,tempo.com,tempo.pt,tameteo.com###meteored_share` | | SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt | [11315](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L11315) | `…,theweather.net,tempo.com,tempo.pt,meteored.*,…##.shared` | | SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt | [13185](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L13185) | `tempo.com,tiempo.com##.botonera > span.boton:has(> span.shared)` | | SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt | [1943](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt#L1943) | `tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*##.tappx-ad` | | SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt | [1944](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt#L1944) | `tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*##.meteored-ads` | Only the `body` rule visibly breaks the site today. The others hide generic class names such as `.shared`, which could hide parts of the new site later. We've already guarded against this on our side with a CSS fix which keeps the page full width even when that rule applies. The report is so AdGuard removes the rules for everyone. 2. Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Reproduced the reporter's large red donation pop-up on theconversation.com/us:⁠ it is a native modal <⁠dialog⁠> that opens on load, dims the page and blocks clicks and wheel scrolling until its own close button is used. The fix is a trusted-click-element scriptlet that dismisses that dialog (plain CSS hiding leaves the native modal open and the page inert), but apply_rule never returned "verified" — the vision review rejected it once for pre-existing unloaded lazy images and once for the separate in-flow donation banner — so it goes to a maintainer unverified.

## Candidate for review

`theconversation.com#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', 'dialog > section > button[aria-label="button.close"]')`

AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never returned verified:⁠ both permitted runs ended environmentExperiment 'inconclusive' with empty failedCandidateChecks, and the third submission was refused as duplicate_candidate. Run 1's review found the pop-up resolved, remainingInstances empty and no ad-layout residue, but flagged pageIntegrity 'regressed' for lower-page article/video/newsletter images; run 2's own settlement evidence shows those same panels unloaded in the before tile, i.e. pre-existing lazy-loading, not candidate damage (run 2:⁠ pageIntegrity 'unclear', observedDamage empty). Run 2 instead counted the separate in-flow 'Join the 1,746 readers…' red donation banner as the same family once the pop-up was closed; the reporter's screenshot shows only the blocking pop-up. Mechanism is proven by the interaction rehearsal (click intercepted and page not scrollable while the dialog is open, both fine after it is closed), so the rule still needs a maintainer's verification.

- Join the 1,746 readers who give monthly to fund fact-based journalism / I'll pitch in — Full-width red donation self-promotion banner with white headline text and a white 'I'll pitch in' button, located between the article grid and the next feature card. ### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [NSFW] [https://hanime.tv/videos/hentai/shounen-ga-otona-ni-natta-natsu-4](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fhanime.tv%2Fvideos%2Fhentai%2Fshounen-ga-otona-ni-natta-natsu-4) ### Comment > Problem: AdGuard Advanced Protection breaks video playback despite website allowlisting and denied extension permissions > > Problem description > > I am experiencing an issue with the AdGuard Safari extension on iOS where embedded video players on hanime.tv become unresponsive when Advanced Protection is enabled. > > The video thumbnail and play button load normally, but tapping the play button does nothing. Long-pressing the play button brings up Safari’s image context menu, including the option to save the image to Photos. > > I have isolated the issue to the main AdGuard Safari extension responsible for Advanced Protection. All six standard AdGuard Safari content blockers can remain enabled without affecting video playback. > > Steps to reproduce > > 1. Enable all AdGuard Safari extensions, including the main AdGuard extension. > 2. Set the main extension’s website permissions to automatically allow access to other websites. > 3. Add hanime.tv to AdGuard’s Safari allowlist. > 4. Explicitly deny the AdGuard extension access to hanime.tv through Safari’s website-specific extension permissions. > 5. Open the website and attempt to play a video. > > Actual behavior > > The video player remains unresponsive despite the website being allowlisted and the extension being explicitly denied access to the domain. > > Interestingly, if I change the global website permission setting to Ask and manually deny access to the affected website, video playback works normally. > > However, as soon as I change the global permission setting to Always Allow for other websites, video playback stops working again, even though the affected website’s individual permission remains set to Deny. > > Expected behavior > > AdGuard should respect website-specific extension permissions and its internal Safari allowlist regardless of the global website permission setting. > > Advanced Protection should remain enabled on all other websites while being excluded from the affected website without requiring me to manually approve every new website I visit. > > Troubleshooting already performed > > * Disabled the main AdGuard Safari extension while keeping all six standard content blockers enabled — video playback works. > * Set global extension permissions to Ask and manually denied access to the affected website — video playback works. > * Set global extension permissions to Always Allow while denying access to the affected website — video playback fails. > * Added the affected domain to AdGuard’s Safari allowlist — issue persists. > * Tested a custom $jsinject exception — issue persists. > * Added custom $document and $elemhide exception rules. > * Reset Safari extension permissions — issue persists. > * Tested video playback in Aloha Browser — video playback works normally. > > Current configuration > > * Operating system: iOS 27.2.1 > * Browser: Safari > * DNS implementation: AdGuard > * DNS server: Cloudflare DNS (DNS-over-HTTPS) > * DNS filters: > * HaGeZi Multi PRO mini > * HaGeZi Threat Intelligence Feeds mini > * Divested Fingerprinting Blocklist > * Safari content blockers: All six enabled > * Advanced Protection: Enabled > > Additional information > > The issue appears to be isolated to the main AdGuard Safari extension rather than DNS protection or the standard Safari content blockers. > > Could this be an issue with Advanced Protection not respecting website-specific permissions, an interaction with cross-origin video frames, or a Safari extension permission bug? > > I would appreciate assistance identifying the underlying cause and finding a permanent solution that allows Advanced Protection to remain enabled globally while respecting individual website exclusions. ### [NSFW] Screenshots [Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/mqlfnfglqdcwoscsw4wcsw8kowc80c46k5kwu83dwc.png?nc=1) [Screenshot 1 with AdGuard disabled](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/o8zisnj76f4w8o8w0448co4sosksckscphgbr11pu8.png?nc=1) ### System configuration | Information | Value | |-------------|-------| AdGuard product: | AdGuard for iOS v1.0 System version: | `IOS 27` License type: | paid Advanced protection: | enabled Filters: | **Ad blocking:**

issue.title: Remove Adguard rules for tempo.com, which has a new owner and thus different content
issue.body: ### Prerequisites - [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml); - [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue; - [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date; - [x] Browser version is up-to-date; - [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue. ### What product do you use? Other ad blocker ### AdGuard version Helium built-in ad blocker ### What type of problem have you encountered? Website or app doesn't work properly ### Which browser(s) do you use? other (specify in comment below) ### Which device do you use? Desktop ### Where is the problem encountered? https://tempo.com/blog/introducing-mercator/ ### Ad Blocking AdGuard Base filter ### Privacy _No response_ ### Social Widgets _No response_ ### Annoyances AdGuard Cookie Notices filter ### Security _No response_ ### Other _No response_ ### DNS filters _No response_ ### Language-specific _No response_ ### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled? _No response_ ### Add your comment and screenshots 1. **tempo.com has changed owners. The Meteored rules for it now break the site and should drop `tempo.com`.** tempo.com used to be Meteored's Italian weather site. Since Nov 17, 2026 it is the website of Tempo, a payments company, and has no Meteored code. The Meteored rules still apply to it, and one of them breaks the layout. **Breaking rule** (AdGuard Cookie Notices filter): ``` yourweather.co.uk,tempo.com,daswetter.com#$#body { position: absolute !important; } ``` This rule shrinks `` to its content width (1320px in a 1989px window). The fixed header stays centred on the full window, the article is centred on only the left part, and the area to the right of the body is never painted, so it shows as a black block. Turning the blocker off fixes it. Safari, which doesn't have the rule, shows the page correctly. Applying the rule in plain Chromium reproduces the same broken layout. Browser: Helium (Chromium-based) on macOS, with its built-in ad blocker and the AdGuard lists above. **Please remove `tempo.com` from these rules.** They all target Meteored markup. The other domains stay as they are. | File | Line | Rule | |---|---|---| | AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt | [10892](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L10892) | `yourweather.co.uk,tempo.com,daswetter.com#$##gpdr { display: none !important; }` | | AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt | [10893](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L10893) | `yourweather.co.uk,tempo.com,daswetter.com#$#body { position: absolute !important; }` (breaks layout) | | AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt | [1590](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt#L1590) | `yourweather.co.uk,theweather.net,tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*##.descarga-app` | | AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt | [5311](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt#L5311) | `tiempo.com,meteored.*,theweather.net,yourweather.co.uk,tempo.pt,tempo.com##.modulo-suscripcion` | | MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt | [1712](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/MobileFilter/sections/specific_web.txt#L1712) | `yourweather.co.uk,theweather.net,tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*#$#.pie-pagina { margin-bottom: 0 !important; }` | | SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt | [6294](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L6294) | `yourweather.co.uk,theweather.net,meteored.*,tempo.com,tempo.pt,tameteo.com###meteored_share` | | SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt | [11315](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L11315) | `…,theweather.net,tempo.com,tempo.pt,meteored.*,…##.shared` | | SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt | [13185](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L13185) | `tempo.com,tiempo.com##.botonera > span.boton:has(> span.shared)` | | SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt | [1943](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt#L1943) | `tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*##.tappx-ad` | | SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt | [1944](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4812eff50c6ddf22a0a93b19014ac9d732ed18ca/SpanishFilter/sections/specific.txt#L1944) | `tempo.pt,tempo.com,tiempo.com,meteored.*##.meteored-ads` | Only the `body` rule visibly breaks the site today. The others hide generic class names such as `.shared`, which could hide parts of the new site later. We've already guarded against this on our side with a CSS fix which keeps the page full width even when that rule applies. The report is so AdGuard removes the rules for everyone. 2. Screenshots **Screenshot 1: tempo.com blog post with the rule applied (black area on the right)** ### Privacy - [x] I agree to follow this condition

did.kr provides a chat widget that businesses embed on their own websites. The Tracking Protection rule `||did.kr^$third-party` blocks the whole domain, so on those sites the chat widget cannot open.

Reproduced with AdGuard Browser Extension 5.5.4.82 (AdGuard Tracking Protection filter 2.1.16.18) on a site that embeds the widget: the chat shows an error and its requests to did.kr are blocked. Disabling AdGuard fixes it. We can share an example site privately if needed. Browser: Chrome 156, macOS.

All tracking from the widget now goes to separate hosts. The widget requests that remain on did.kr and cdn.did.kr only run the widget:

- Tracking: track.did.kr, analytics.did.kr
- Widget: did.kr, cdn.did.kr

Could `||did.kr^$third-party` be replaced with `||track.did.kr^$third-party` and `||analytics.did.kr^$third-party`? Visitors stay protected from tracking, and the widget keeps working.

### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — 4ppl.pl shows a first-party cookie-consent card (body ⁠> div[⁠data-cookie-card="true"]⁠, randomized class o-PmhG_card) fixed at the bottom-left over the hero/logo/stats area, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter does not cover. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule on the card's stable `data-cookie-card` attribute verified in the reporter profile:⁠ card hidden, symptom resolved, page integrity intact. ## Rule `4ppl.pl##div[data-cookie-card]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction policy:⁠ a cookie-notice annoyance is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall and not self-promotion, so no repository rule blocks rule generation for it. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's purpose covers cookie notifications; the reported card is a domain-specific cookie notice, so the fix belongs in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. No existing rule covered 4ppl.pl and the only shared rule hiding the same element would also hide legitimate page content on this site, so a new narrow domain rule is the appropriate fix. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/96d50f6731ed801898962a90832f5f96b1b88eba/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Under the heading `! The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported "spam on every click" was not reproducible:⁠ dasfootball.com's only ad loader is a page-injected Profiton popunder script (https:⁠//chinar.roamersitemise.com/rxLodV2fZ0Enfu3x/159586, id="profiton-pops"), already blocked on every load by an existing AdGuard Base filter regex rule, and six click rehearsals on the homepage and a match page opened no popup or tab; full-page vision found no ad instance or placeholder. No new rule is needed.

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule closes this report:⁠ a popunder ad served by a third party is an ad that the instruction says gets a rule like any other ad ('Ads for other companies get a rule like any other ad'), so rule generation is allowed. The close recommendation rests only on live evidence that the reported spam window could not be reproduced, because the popunder loader it needs is already blocked by an existing AdGuard Base filter rule.

## Artifacts

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"bb2116de81ff2f2eb4e52cf8c7979ad31c9653ba9764d103cbd77cd3d0d1bfb2"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

Variety's "Disable Your Adblocker" wall does reproduce on the reported URL under the reporter's filter selection, but it is an Admiral "Failsafe" overlay injected by an inline page-head script, and one click on its "Continue without disabling" button removes it and unlocks the fully loaded homepage without disabling the blocker. No captured request proves a detector script to target, and AdGuard's filter policy excludes ad-blocker messages that let the user proceed to the content, so I recommend closing without a rule and handing the anti-adblock report to a maintainer.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "We do not block ad blocker detection messages that satisfy at least one of the following criteria:⁠ ... They provide an alternative to disabling an ad blocker given that this alternative does not put the users' privacy or security at risk ... They allow the user to proceed to the website's content" — the reported Variety overlay is exactly such a message:⁠ one click on its "Continue without disabling" button removed it and the full homepage content became visible, with no consent, payment, permission or reload required. Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Anti-adblock walls:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The overlay is built by an inline script embedded in the served HTML (document.scripts[⁠20]⁠, sets window._afsr, renders an Admiral "Failsafe" template); no captured request demonstrates a detector script that a rule could target. The blocked third-party requests that plausibly belong to the same vendor (jsstore ge.js blocked by Tracking Protection, zodiacglass.com/files/.../enu.js) cannot be proven to drive this wall, so the report goes to a maintainer instead of a rule. Run instruction:⁠ the agent never closes an issue; this outcome recommends closing and a maintainer decides.

## Artifacts

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — geeksforgeeks.org loads a full-screen in-house promo modal (.saleModalPanel, fixed 1920x1080 with a rgba(0,0,0,0.4) dimming backdrop) that covers the homepage, matching the reporter's screenshot; the domain-scoped hide rule geeksforgeeks.org#⁠#⁠.saleModalPanel was verified in the AdGuard extension session (modal visible in phase B, hidden in phase C, page integrity intact, no residue). Rule belongs in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt next to the site's existing self-promo rules. ## Rule `geeksforgeeks.org##.saleModalPanel` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction:⁠ the site's own advertising (self-promotion) gets a rule proposed for AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt, with the maintainer deciding whether it is annoying enough. Not a paywall, not a consent/CMP gate, not an anti-adblock wall (no detector script was captured in the page requests), and not a scam/phishing page, so none of the instruction's close/hand-off rules applies. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f971ffa342b5a4b0e5e008c8fcbb9f30852e0396/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) Under the heading `! SECTION: Self-promo - Regular rules`, before [line 3534](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f971ffa342b5a4b0e5e008c8fcbb9f30852e0396/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt#L3534). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — topgear.es shows a Marfeel/Didomi cookie-consent modal ("Acepta para leer gratis y sin límites", "Rechazar y pagar" / "Aceptar y cerrar") with a full-page dark backdrop that also locks `body` scrolling; the shared `##.mrf-cmp` rule leaves that backdrop, so the validated fix is the site-scoped CSS-injection rule `topgear.es#$#.mrf-cmp, #mrf-popup, body { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }` in the Cookie Notices filter, which hides the overlay and releases the lock. Note `.mrf-cmp` is inert under these declarations and kept only as the Marfeel-CMP anchor shared with der-postillon.com/ghacks.net. ## Rule `topgear.es#$#.mrf-cmp, #mrf-popup, body { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The gate is a cookie-consent notice (Marfeel CMP backed by Didomi) over content that is already served and readable behind it — the dialog offers 'Acepta para leer gratis y sin límites' — so it is not a content paywall, which is the only annoyance case the instruction closes without a rule. It is not an anti-adblock wall:⁠ no detector script, no request to disable the ad blocker; the reporter's own text and the captured network inventory show a consent dialog only. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's documented purpose is to block cookie notices and consent-management-platform requests, so the fix belongs to rule generation in that filter. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e9d52afa63a9f342c2a94320628e86c433805345/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Regular rules`, before [line 407](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e9d52afa63a9f342c2a94320628e86c433805345/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L407). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Trackers) [https://t3.codes/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft3.codes%2F) ### Comment > Please add `||ingest.t3.codes^` to the AdGuard DNS filter (and EasyPrivacy if relevant). > > **What it is:** `ingest.t3.codes` is the analytics endpoint of T3 Code, an open-source desktop app for coding agents. It is a first-party proxy in front of PostHog: the app POSTs events to `https://ingest.t3.codes/batch/`. Telemetry is on by default. > > **Sources:** > - Telemetry docs: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/docs/user/telemetry.md > - `apps/server/src/telemetry/AnalyticsService.ts`: `T3CODE_POSTHOG_HOST` defaults to `https://ingest.t3.codes`, events are sent to `/batch/` > > **Why existing rules miss it:** it is a custom subdomain proxied through Cloudflare, with no CNAME to posthog.com, so PostHog rules and CNAME uncloaking don't catch it. It is not in the AdGuard DNS filter or EasyPrivacy as of 2026-11-18. > > **Screenshot:** the AdGuard DNS Default server (94.140.14.14) blocks google-analytics.com (0.0.0.0) but resolves ingest.t3.codes, and a request over AdGuard DNS-over-HTTPS reaches the endpoint. > > **Breakage:** none expected. The app works normally with this host blocked. Please block only this subdomain, not t3.codes. ### Screenshots

issue.title: Remove AI filters from the Other Annoyances
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

AdGuard Other Annoyances filter blocks AI features such as Google Search Overview.

### Proposed solution

Since AdGuard already offers an AI-annoyance blocking filter list (Stevo's AI Blocklist) I think that rules blocking AI should be removed from the Other Annoyances filter list. Additionally, while the filter provides many useful rules that block unnecessary clutter and other features, some users use these AI features and don't want them blocked, but still want the blocking power of the rest of the filter list. All in all, I think this should be done because there is already a specialized list for this specific purpose that is more comprehensive, and some users want to enable Other Annoyances without blocking AI features.

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — map.baidu.com shows a message-center promo/ad carousel card (the 地图互动实验室 creative with the yellow 广告 label in the report) over the map; the rule map.baidu.com#⁠#⁠#⁠message-panel hides it and was verified in the reporter's settings session (symptom resolved, page intact). It is filed in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt next to baidu.com#⁠#⁠#⁠con-ceiling-wrapper because the promoted feature is Baidu Maps' own, but the creative carries an 广告 label and the slot is filled by the site's ad-ops API — if a maintainer judges a third party advertises there, the same rule belongs in ChineseFilter/sections/specific.txt. ## Rule `map.baidu.com###message-panel` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction gives advertising and site self-promotion a rule; this report is neither a paywall, a consent-banner problem, nor an anti-adblock wall (no detector script appeared in the captured requests; the panel is a promo/ad carousel, not a filter-detection dialog). The promoted product is a Baidu Maps feature and every creative host in the request inventory is Baidu-owned, so the element is the site's own advertising; the instruction sends that to AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt with the blocking decision left to a maintainer. No reproduction-based closure applies:⁠ the reported widget is live and unfiltered, only the specific creative differs on this egress. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/6a3dfe9625cfcfbfb4a0dbc7fbf2ec252fd20beb/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) Under the heading `! Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — daskochrezept.de serves its ad slots as empty ANZEIGE placeholders once the Base filter blocks its ad engine, and the existing shared rule einfachkochen.de,einfachbacken.de#⁠#⁠.stf-slot (GermanFilter/sections/specific.txt, project group lines 622-624) hides exactly that framework; the candidate daskochrezept.de#⁠#⁠.stf-slot hid all six slots with page integrity intact, but the vision review rejected it over the page's own footer spacing (measured as 180 px in both baseline and filtered states), so it goes to a maintainer to add daskochrezept.de to every line of that group.

## Candidate for review

`daskochrezept.de##.stf-slot`

GermanFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule ran twice on the locked baseline:⁠ phase C hid all six .stf-slot containers (targetVisibleCount 0), pageIntegrity intact, observedDamage empty, all nine BEFORE symptom instances gone; visualReview still returned `rejected` / symptom `not_resolved` / adLayoutResidue `present` and the experiment stayed `inconclusive` with no failedCandidateChecks. Its only remaining instance is a blank strip above the footer, measured as the page's own spacing:⁠ 454 px baseline gap with a 274 px slot inside it vs 180 px with nothing occupying it after filtering (40 px section margin + 140 px main padding/parent spacing present in both states); a vision pass on that exact tile shows plain white background, no placeholder. The selector is the shared sibling-site rule at GermanFilter/sections/specific.txt lines 622-624, so the family's established fix only needs its domain list extended.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"cef69ad0784083df70807b1351e084918d429b5c6513d3dee5c141d64e367b3f"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — crazygames.com's game page shows an Admiral adblock-recovery wall ("Ads Keep Every Game Free"), confirmed present in the current prepared extension session, and it only appears with filtering; blocking the Admiral loader timeprince.com for this site removed the wall and all its requests in every experiment phase, but the dedicated review would not confirm the fix because the embedded game never renders in the headless browser — the same blank player appears unfiltered and after the site's own "Continue without disabling" dismissal. Carried for human review as the candidate rule.

## Candidate for review

`||timeprince.com^$domain=crazygames.com`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never rejected it (environmentExperiment inconclusive, failedCandidateChecks empty) and its network check is verified:⁠ filtered baseline made 10-11 allowed timeprince.com requests with the Admiral wall present; with the candidate 0 allowed / 2 blocked and no wall. Binding vision could not verify it:⁠ one run judged the wall resolved with no remaining wall instances but called page integrity regressed for pre-existing unloaded 'Play next' thumbnails; other runs kept the withheld game player in scope and saw it still blank. That blank player is an environment limit, not the rule's effect:⁠ it is equally blank in the unfiltered phase A and after the site's own 'Continue without disabling' dismissal in a live rehearsal. File BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt next to the crazygames.com anti-adblock entries (lines 3887-3890), not in the shared crazygames/shellshock/minijuegos group at 4627-4631.

## Still visible after the rule

- Combat Online 2 — game player area above the player control bar (large light-gray rectangle) — The content gated by the anti-adblock wall is still withheld:⁠ the entire game player region is a featureless light-gray placeholder block with no game canvas, no loading state and no playable content. The dimmed overlay and 'Ads Keep Every Game Free' modal themselves are not shown in this state, but the game they gated is still absent, so the same symptom remains.
- Main game/player panel to the right of the left navigation rail and left of the 'Play next' sidebar, above the 'Combat Online 2' toolbar — The entire game player region is an empty flat gray field with no game, no video and no playable content rendered in it; the game that the anti-adblock wall gates is still withheld here. The 'Ads Keep Every Game Free' modal and dimmed backdrop are not visible in this viewport, so the gate is absent from view but the withheld gameplay it produces remains, and the page still presents a non-functional empty player to the user.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45602422522

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Environment:⁠ browser_extension — select_environment accepted once (state "ready", filterBaseline executable, 18 official AdGuard lists; the reporter's third-party Polish/EasyList catalogs listed as skippedSources). A re-submission of the identical selection to clear the gate was refused with `environment_locked`/selectedKind browser_extension, so the selection is locked, yet open_page reports gate `environment-pending`. That contradiction is recorded, not resolved by a switch. BOUNDED TECHNICAL ATTEMPTS (all spent, no session ever existed):⁠ - fetch_issue #⁠248135 called twice, identical payload. - launch_browser (12+ calls, prepared and control `extension:"none"`) always refused with errorKind `target_url_not_allowed` — "targetUrl must exactly match one of the prompt-safe URLs in fetch_issue" — for every URL the issue carries:⁠ the markdown link-text article URL (and with trailing slash, and host root), the AnonymousRedirect wrapper exactly as written (uppercase percent-encoding), the wrapper with the inner URL unencoded, with lowercase percent-encoding, and fully lowercased host, the wrapper without its query, the issue's own `url` field, the reporter settings import URL verbatim, and the screenshot CDN URL. A separate probe with `settings.kind=defaults_plus_required` showed settings are validated before targetUrl, so the refusal really is the URL allowlist:⁠ not even `issue.url` or the import URL is accepted, which no correct extractor could omit — the prompt-safe list is empty or mis-parsed for this issue. Recorded with report_missing_information. - open_page called three times (the third just now) for the reporter-defined article; every call returns `tool_gated`, gate `environment-pending`, "open_page needs a locked environment; this run has not accepted an environment selection yet". (shortened; the full text is in the run artifacts)

## Missing information

- launch_browser targetUrl allowlist rejects every URL present in fetch_issue: The locked browser_extension environment reports state "ready" with an executable filter baseline, but launch_browser could not start any session:⁠ every targetUrl form taken from fetch_issue #⁠248135 was refused with errorKind "target_url_not_allowed" ("targetUrl must exactly match one of the prompt-safe URLs in fetch_issue"). Tried verbatim:⁠ (1) the markdown link text https:⁠//sportowefakty.wp.pl/pilka-nozna/1285979/real-madryt-odpalil-fajerwerki-gol-niczem-z-gry-komputerowej, (2) the AnonymousRedirect wrapper with uppercase percent-encoding as written in the body, (3) the wrapper with the inner URL unencoded, (4) the wrapper with lowercase percent-encoding, (5) the issue's own url field https:⁠//github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/248135, (6) the import settings URL verbatim, (7) the issue screenshot CDN URL https:⁠//cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/...png?nc=1, plus host-root and trailing-slash/no-scheme variants. Not one was accepted, including the issue URL itself and the reporter import URL, so the prompt-safe allowlist appears to be empty or mis-parsed for this issue. Without a session there is no navigation, no DOM/network/console evidence, no get_applied_rules and no apply_rule; the run cannot verify any candidate and must stay analysis-only. comment.body:
Hello.

To analyze the problem, we need the filtering log.

### How to Record and Export the AdGuard for Android Filtering Log

1. **Fully stop the affected app.** Open Android Settings → Apps → select the affected app → **Force stop**.

2. **Clear the affected app's cache.** Open Android Settings → Apps → select the app → Storage → **Clear cache**.  
   ⚠️ Do not confuse this with **Clear data** — this will delete the app's settings and data.

3. **Clear the AdGuard filtering log.** Open AdGuard → **Statistics → Recent Activity** → tap the three-dot menu → **Clear recent activity**.

4. **Reproduce the issue.** Launch the affected app and perform the actions that cause the issue or make ads appear.

5. **Export the log.** In AdGuard, open **Statistics → Recent Activity** → tap the three-dot menu → **Export**.

6. **Save the log.** In the pop-up window, tap **Share** and choose a convenient way to save or share the file.

7. **Submit the log for analysis (choose one of the following options):**
   - **Option 1:** Attach the file to a comment or a new issue on GitHub.
   - **Option 2:** Upload the file to a file-sharing service that allows you to delete it, for example, https://www.transfr.me/. Email `filters@adguard.com` with the file link and the issue link.

**Important:** Do not clear the app's data or stop AdGuard while reproducing the issue.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The promo card the reporter marked on the Orange Data receipt page is an RMEX ad-network creative (app.rmex.io creative/click/loader requests, image labeled "Реклама", link rel="sponsored"), and the site's existing rules only hid the other RMEX promo cards. Proposing `||app.rmex.io^$domain=cheques-lk.orangedata.ru` in CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt, inserted at line 241 right after the site's existing RMEX rules; apply_rule verified the banner gone with the receipt, QR code and page layout intact. ## Rule `||app.rmex.io^$domain=cheques-lk.orangedata.ru` ## Policy rationale Filter policy:⁠ "Ads for other companies get a rule like any other ad, wherever the site serves them from" — the banner is a third-party ad-network creative (RMEX click/impression/creative endpoints, alt="Реклама", rel="sponsored"), not the site's self-promotion and not a paywall or anti-adblock gate. The report is not closed by any listed policy rule (not a paywall, not a consent banner, not a scam page); a rule is the right resolution. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c108caaf1558844cc9bd3d3da1f3b6809b28fe29/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Specific rules`, before [line 241](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c108caaf1558844cc9bd3d3da1f3b6809b28fe29/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt#L241). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — bird.rent shows a fullscreen "Відкрий bird у застосунку" app-promo dialog on every load, covering the whole Kyiv map; it is served in the page's own HTML with no request behind it. The scoped element-hiding rule bird.rent#⁠#⁠.redirector dialog.modal was validated through the filtering proxy (interstitial hidden, map renders and works, page integrity intact), so it is proposed for AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt. ## Rule `bird.rent##.redirector dialog.modal` ## Policy rationale The run instruction states no rule that closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not self-promotion — it is a popup encouraging visitors to install the site's mobile app, which the AdGuard filter policy explicitly assigns to the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter. The AdGuard Mobile App Banners policy limitation (header/menu banners that are not animated and occupy little space) does not apply:⁠ this is a full-viewport interstitial that withholds the entire map. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a8289ccf6720879287faa3078520f67846a094b1/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) Under the heading `! SECTION: Mobile apps - Regular rules`, before [line 21](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a8289ccf6720879287faa3078520f67846a094b1/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt#L21). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"e54b17ee021932848345053a1991f48842f52e5643d5372e51fc17adf9ac8f97"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported large blank spaces between posts on wykop.pl/mikroblog do not occur on the live filtered page:⁠ all 15 ad placements, including the stream slots between posts, are collapsed to zero size and the feed renders normally in both light and night themes, while the repo already hides these containers and blocks the site's ad API. Recommend closing as not reproducible — no filter rule is needed.

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall (no ad-blocker-detection wall or popup is shown on the page), and the ads involved are third-party/own placements that are already blocked by the shipped filters rather than self-promotion to route to self-promo.txt. Rule generation is therefore not blocked. The report says no rule is needed because the reported leftover blank space does not occur on the live filtered page, so the run recommends closing it; the run instruction states the agent never closes an issue and a maintainer decides.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45664845158

issue.title: New set of Instagram tracking parameters
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I reported in #244642 that Instagram has been using multiple tracking parameter names instead of their traditional ones (`igshid`, `igsh`, `igsi`). That got addressed in 2f8d5f3 and for a while, it seemed solved.

But now, I've suddenly been seeing new tracking parameter names. We don't have enough data to be sure, but it seems they may be using a set of ten or so names at a time, then after a while they change to a new set. Luckily, they still follow the same name pattern (`[a-z]{4}`).

## Details
I've been keeping track of every new parameter I've encountered since mid-October. Caveat: this is very unscientific and just from my perspective as someone with multiple friends who send links frequently.

Since I started keeping track on Oct 17, I saw 5 new ones between then and Oct 26, then nothing new until Nov 19, then 5 new ones between then and today. I haven't noted when I see old parameters I've seen before, but from memory, I don't recall seeing any old ones in the last several days. They may have switched them out entirely.

In any case, the new ones I've observed so far are `'bqrl', 'cnvx', 'evlk', 'lqvp', 'obrf'`.

### Proposed solution

It may be time to adopt @stdedos' [proposed solution](/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/244642#issuecomment-6273749064) that uses regex:
```adblock
||instagram.com/reel/$removeparam=/^[a-z]{4}=/
||instagram.com/p/$removeparam=/^[a-z]{4}=/
```

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — vaidoo.de serves a Real Cookie Banner consent dialog (div[⁠consent-skip-blocker="1"]⁠ ⁠> dialog.ac414-2, z-index 999999) that covers the viewport and scroll-locks html/body; no baseline rule acted on it. A domain-scoped trusted-click-element scriptlet that clicks "Weiter ohne Einwilligung" inside the RCB container was verified in the browser (banner gone, page content visible, integrity intact). The expression is identical to the shared rule on line 375, so a maintainer may prefer adding vaidoo.de to that line's domain list instead of the new line placed in the "! real_cookie_banner" group. ## Rule `vaidoo.de#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', 'div[consent-skip-blocker="1"] div[class*="-ext-"] > a[href="#"]:not([id])', '!cookie:/real_cookie_banner-v/, containsText:Weiter ohne Einwilligung')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance on a German site; the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's stated purpose covers cookie notices and CMP requests, and the KB allows non-essential consent to be declined by default. No policy rule closes it:⁠ the page gates nothing behind the dialog (no paywall), and it is not an anti-adblock wall — the visible element is a plain Real Cookie Banner consent dialog, with no ad-blocker message in the DOM or the captured requests. The fix fits the repository's existing real_cookie_banner shared scriptlet family in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, so it is a shared-rule extension rather than a site-specific invention. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f206590317e2fb2ea0c93c7f9d9a3a7017c67fde/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 375](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f206590317e2fb2ea0c93c7f9d9a3a7017c67fde/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L375). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45683661953 Automated analysis against filters at `f206590`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — 24ores.gr serves a first-party bottom cookie-consent card (`div#ck[aria-label="Cookies"]`, Google Analytics text, "Απόρριψη"/"Αποδοχή"); hiding it removed the prompt with the article page intact (apply_rule verified). Fix:⁠ add 24ores.gr to the existing shared rule on line 4474 of AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt (`codeengineers.com,outletmoto.com,docs.blackbox.chat##div[aria-label="Cookies"]`), keeping the repo convention of putting the new domain at the beginning:⁠ `24ores.gr,codeengineers.com,outletmoto.com,docs.blackbox.chat##div[aria-label="Cookies"]`. ## Rule `24ores.gr##div[aria-label="Cookies"]` ## Policy rationale The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy states that in most cases simply hiding the corresponding cookie notice is sufficient, which is exactly what was done. Maintainer rule:⁠ when the fix fits an existing shared rule, add the reported domain to that rule instead of writing a new one; line 4474 of cookies_specific.txt is such a shared rule and is not a project group. The notice is not a content gate:⁠ the article, media and scrolling stayed usable, so the candidate-rule policy forbidding hiding of gated placeholders does not apply. No paywall, anti-adblock or self-promotion element is involved. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f206590317e2fb2ea0c93c7f9d9a3a7017c67fde/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 4474](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f206590317e2fb2ea0c93c7f9d9a3a7017c67fde/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L4474). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45683240917 Automated analysis against filters at `f206590`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"dac9ff4f49f11129931b5c12ffe17e741212ac451c98384fead47bf21c824a55"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

Reproduced the reported anti-adblock prompt on www⁠.kgw.com:⁠ Admiral's 'Help Us Thrive:⁠ Please Allow Ads' dialog covers the page and locks scrolling while the reporter's filters are active. No rule is recommended because the dialog offers 'Continue without supporting us', which dismisses it in one click, releases the scroll lock and leaves the site fully usable — the AdGuard filter policy excludes detection messages that let users proceed to the content.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

AdGuard filter policy (this run's role document), 'Limitations and exceptions':⁠ 'We do not block ad blocker detection messages that satisfy at least one of the following criteria:⁠ ... They allow the user to proceed to the website's content.' Observed in the reporter-profile session:⁠ the Admiral dialog offers 'Continue without supporting us'; one click on it removed the overlay, cleared the inline overflow:⁠hidden from html and body, and left the page fully usable and scrollable with no re-appearance during the session — the message lets the user proceed to the content, so the policy excludes blocking it. The same section blocks walls only when they 'aggressively insist on disabling or removing the ad blocker or effectively prevent using the website'; this one does not effectively prevent using the website, and no misleading copy, malvertising source or privacy violation was observed.

## Artifacts

The same selector is already used by the shared rule `explainx.ai,tech-insider.org##aside[aria-label="Newsletter signup"]` on line 551 of AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt, so the maintainer should add linuxblog.io to that rule's domain list there. ## Rule `linuxblog.io##aside[aria-label="Newsletter signup"]` ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance-class site newsletter/PDF subscription sheet; none of the run instruction's closing rules (paywalls, anti-adblock walls, non-anti-adblock scams) applies, and the page's own subscription popups are already handled in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups. No gate over content is involved:⁠ the sheet overlays an already-loaded article (cookie/consent gates and paywalls would be left alone), so hiding the overlay is a valid annoyance fix rather than hiding a user's signal for a broken function. The fix extends an existing two-domain shared selector rule instead of creating a project group, as the maintainer rules require. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 551](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt#L551). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"092338cfa1cea53646eca009208745c79b1dd4ac6f2a3835f5182e8d4efdb1fb"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The bankinggeek.com cookie notice is a first-party Real Cookie Banner dialog rendered \~15-20 s after load from /wp-content/f112afd146e9f38d5cbd5448e7b347cb/; the repository's real_cookie_banner click-scriptlet did not fire on that delay, while the first-party path rule removed the modal, backdrop and scroll lock in the verified phase but the vision review left page integrity "unclear", so it is carried for human review.

## Candidate for review

`||bankinggeek.com/wp-content/f112afd146e9f38d5cbd5448e7b347cb/`

AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule did not reject it (failedCandidateChecks empty):⁠ phase C showed the Real Cookie Banner dialog, its backdrop and the body scroll lock gone, with no remaining instances, no observed damage and no ad layout residue. The dedicated vision review returned verdict "inconclusive" because pageIntegrity was "unclear":⁠ static before/after captures of the first-party request being blocked cannot show that the site's consent-dependent functions still work, so the experiment could not be marked verified. Placement:⁠ beginning of the Regular-rules block of AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt (before line 407, next to the ||ikea.com/pl/pl/cookieconsent/v2/scripts/ first-party CMP path rule). Note for the maintainer:⁠ the hashed /wp-content/<⁠hash⁠>/ directory is per-install, so the rule will need refreshing if the plugin's asset directory changes.

## Missing information

- trusted-click-element parameter semantics (delay/extraToken) not covered by the served rule-guidance documents: The scriptlet guidance served by lookup_rule_guidance (create-own-filters.md scriptlet sections, filter-policy.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) explains trusted scriptlets only in general terms; it does not describe the parameter list or the retry/timeout behaviour of `trusted-click-element`, which the repository's `! real_cookie_banner` family in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt (lines 372-379) relies on. issue.title: New set of Instagram tracking parameters
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

I reported in #244642 that Instagram has been using multiple tracking parameter names instead of their traditional ones (`igshid`, `igsh`, `igsi`). That got addressed in 2f8d5f3 and for a while, it seemed solved.

But now, I've suddenly been seeing new tracking parameter names. We don't have enough data to be sure, but it seems they may be using a set of ten or so names at a time, then after a while they change to a new set. Luckily, they still follow the same name pattern (`[a-z]{4}`).

#### Details
I've been keeping track of every new parameter I've encountered since mid-October. Caveat: this is very unscientific and just from my perspective as someone with multiple friends who send links frequently.

Since I started keeping track on Oct 17, I saw 5 new ones between then and Oct 26, then nothing new until Nov 19, then 7 new ones between then and today. I haven't noted when I see old parameters I've seen before, but from memory, I don't recall seeing any old ones in the last several days. They may have switched them out entirely.

In any case, the new ones I've observed so far are `'bqrl', 'cnvx', 'evlk', 'lqvp', 'obrf', 'gwpx', 'jplx'`.

#### Update 2026-11-25
Updated to add two new parameters I saw just after creating the issue.

### Proposed solution

It may be time to adopt @stdedos' [proposed solution](/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/244642#issuecomment-6273749064) that uses regex:
```adblock
||instagram.com/reel/$removeparam=/^[a-z]{4}=/
||instagram.com/p/$removeparam=/^[a-z]{4}=/
```

### Additional information

_No response_

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Taste of Home shows a full-screen Admiral anti-adblock gate ("It looks like you are using an adblocker.") driven by an obfuscated inline activator that loads its detector from berrytots.com; blocking that third-party loader on this site removed the gate in the verified A/B/C experiment with page integrity intact. Reviewer notes:⁠ the live creative also carries a "Continue without disabling" control, which the generic filter-policy exclusions may weigh, and the vendor's script names a fallback host (succeedscene.com) that was requested in the candidate phase. ## Rule `||berrytots.com^$domain=tasteofhome.com` Leftover layout: the page still reserves space where the advertising was. A network rule cannot collapse it; add a cosmetic rule if the gap matters. ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is an anti-adblock wall whose detector script is present in the page's captured requests (berrytots.com /static/js/n3vlu9qhb/x05, injected by the inline #⁠admiral-activator-js), which is the run instruction's condition for writing an anti-adblock rule. No instruction rule closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not self-promotion, and it is an ad-blocker detection wall rather than a consent-banner breakage or a scam page. The wall overlays and dims the whole homepage until the reader allows ads; whether the live 'Continue without disabling' control makes it non-blocking is the maintainer's call and is surfaced in the summary. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Regular rules`, before [line 1279](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt#L1279). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45700438910 Automated analysis against filters at `a341349`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — kia.com's Ukrainian Sorento page shows a first-party cookie-consent sheet (#⁠kia-cookie-consent) covering the lower half of the mobile viewport; the reported domain belongs on the existing shared cookie-notice rule `div[class*="cookie-consent"]` in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt (line 6709), whose domain list becomes `kia.com,scentcorner.pl,otomiinsatu.com,organoid.farm,jivo.ru,e-kinopodbaranami.pl`. The domain-scoped candidate was verified live:⁠ the sheet is gone, no remaining instances, page integrity intact and the page still scrolls. ## Rule `kia.com##div[class*="cookie-consent"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction closes only paywalls, anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script, and unrelated scam pages; this report is a cookie-notice annoyance (explicitly out of the anti-adblock rule, since a notice about consent is a cookie-consent problem), so no rule in the instruction blocks rule generation. AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy covers exactly this:⁠ hiding the notice is the standard method when the site functions without an explicit cookie decision, which the live evidence supports (no gated third-party content, no scroll lock, page content visible and interactive behind the sheet). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 6709](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L6709). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45706604663 Automated analysis against filters at `a341349`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — parallels.com showed the site's own "BLACK FRIDAY … Save up to 50%" bar fixed at the top of the viewport (#⁠headersw.promoBanner, position:⁠ fixed, z-index 1000), which the reporter flagged as a sticky self-promotion annoyance. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule that removes the bar together with its 61px placeholder was verified on the reported page:⁠ banner gone, no blank strip, page integrity intact. ## Rule `parallels.com##.promoBanner, .promobanner-placeholder` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy sends the site's own promotion (banners promoting its own products, no third party paying) to AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt; the filter policy document lists 'Block self-promotion of websites' as a purpose of the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter. No policy rule closes or hands off this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not a scam page. The banner promotes Parallels' own product with data-promo-sku="parallels" and no third-party advertiser, so it is self-promotion rather than a third-party ad. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) Under the heading `! <!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"1be25ca0d56d8e533a2755035393c6d550d5013d250d1f3cc4d2f1a91d967455"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The reported "Proszę wyłączyć blokowanie reklam!" anti-adblock wall was absent on the loaded player.radiozet.pl page:⁠ the full-page capture shows only the player's own loading spinner while all other content renders, and no ad-block detector request appears in the captured traffic — only the site's first-party consent/ad stack (rodoguard, OneTrust AutoBlock, Yieldbird, Onnetwork, ez CMP). With no captured detector the anti-adblock policy leaves the decision to a maintainer, who can also test with the reporter's AdGuard Polish filter that the baseline could not load.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, anti-adblock walls:⁠ "write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The captured requests (artifact:⁠har:⁠94432e7a-7662-4f64-ba95-05420d3c2333, artifact:⁠har:⁠ea3508b6-d7c1-45c1-a3f6-acacb245e363) show no ad-block detector:⁠ only first-party consent/ad framework assets on gfx-player.radiozet.pl (rodoguard.eurozet.main.iife.js, Onetrust/AutoBlock.js, Yieldbird.js, Yieldbird-embed-v2.js, Onnetwork.js) and the ez CMP script on static.tokfm.pl. Filter policy, quality requirements:⁠ hiding the player's .preloader placeholder would not restore the gated function (no audio element exists, the player never initializes) and the policy forbids treating a placeholder gate as the fix; no scriptlet target can be named because no detector property or request was observed. Reporter parity is unavailable in the locked baseline:⁠ filterBaseline.skippedSources lists AdGuard Polish as unresolved_name (it holds the radiozet.pl rules in PolishFilter/sections/specific.txt) and the reporter's AdGuard Extra/Popup Blocker userscripts and DNS filtering cannot be reproduced by the proxy, so a maintainer should judge the report with the reporter's configuration. The structured full-page capture of the filtered session reports the reported anti-adblock message absent (reporterSymptomPresence absent, 0 instances) while the player region stays on its own loading spinner, so a maintainer must decide whether the report is already resolved or specific to the reporter's full filter set.

## Missing information

- Reporter's AdGuard Polish filter unavailable in the locked CLI baseline: The accepted adguard_cli environment returned filterBaseline with skippedSources:⁠ {kind:⁠ "unresolved_name", reportedName:⁠ "AdGuard Polish"} plus third-party catalogs EasyList Lithuania and ABPVN List. The reporter's settings include AdGuard Polish, which holds this site's rules (e.g. PolishFilter/sections/specific.txt lines 5257-5266 for radiozet.pl), and the reporter also ran AdGuard Extra and Popup Blocker userscripts plus DNS filtering that the proxy baseline cannot reproduce. Therefore the reporter's exact blocking configuration cannot be recreated to test whether it produces the reported "Proszę wyłączyć blokowanie reklam!" gate.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45724009908

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — All three routes to the reported canva.com design editor redirect to Canva's "Log in or sign up to view this presentation" wall, and the issue's screenshot is an unreadable 52x231 px sliver, so the outlined ad could not be identified; the public canva.com homepage I could reach shows no ads and no ad containers. With no observed ad, no causal request and no selector anchor, no verifiable rule exists — handed over as analysis-only with the sign-in-wall and full-page capture evidence.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Issue screenshot 1 is an unreadable 52×231 px sliver, so the reporter-defined ad target cannot be established: Vision inspection of issue screenshot 1 (cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/r1uvgpmopv4so0sc44ck4ssog8goc4ke7fb8qpgiwg.png) reports an extremely narrow, tall image (\~52x231 px, \~0.23:⁠1) with mirrored/unreadable text, no legible labels, no ad creative, placeholder graphic or bordered box, and only a hand-drawn vertical line with two small circle marks along the left edge outlining a blank strip. No higher-resolution or additional reporter screenshot is provided in the issue, so neither the element the reporter outlined nor the ad it should contain can be identified from the report itself. Combined with the reported page being behind a Canva sign-in wall in this environment, no reporter-defined target is available to anchor a selector.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On www⁠.zendesk.com the only filterable chat-widget element is the fixed "Open chat" launcher that lazy-loads the Zendesk Messenger from static.zdassets.com; the white "AI agent" panel in the reporter's screenshot is painted by the site's own hero animation canvas, which the visual review counted as a remaining widget and rejected the candidate for. The launcher-hiding rule stays browser-unverified and is carried for a maintainer.

## Candidate for review

`zendesk.com##button[aria-label="Open chat"], iframe#launcher`

AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt

Not verified: apply_rule removed the launcher (adElementStatus phaseB 'visible' -⁠> phaseC 'hidden', pageIntegrity intact, observedDamage empty), but the bound visual review returned 'rejected' / symptom 'not_resolved' because it also counted the site's own hero Rive animation - which paints an 'AI agent' chat card inside the CANVAS at x=1329 w=415 h=995 of section#⁠hero, with no matching text anywhere in the DOM - as a remaining chat-widget panel. That card is page content that no rule may hide without destroying the hero, so the review's symptom scope cannot be satisfied by any legitimate rule; environmentExperiment was inconclusive with no failed candidate checks. Suggested placement:⁠ AnnoyancesFilter/Widgets/sections/widgets.txt, section 'Widgets - Chats (specific)' (lines 2053-2272; per-site chat rules sit around lines 2074-2080).

## Still visible after the rule

- Hero image, lower-right over the woman with green headphones — Dark 'AI agent chain of thought' chat panel floating at the lower-right of the hero, overlaying the photo. It shows a sparkle icon, the title, and checklist rows including 'Verify user and reward balance', 'Identify checkout issue', 'Apply discount + update cart', and 'Open Jira issue for follow up'.
- Top-right of the hero photo, overlapping continuation of the lower-right chat overlay — Lower portion of the same dark 'AI agent chain of thought' chat panel is visible at the top-right of this overlapping tile, including checklist rows and 'Open Jira issue for follow up'. This is the continued crop of the panel recorded in the first tile, not a separate page location.
- Bottom-right corner over the hero image — White chat-widget message panel with a Mia avatar and the text “My rewards points are not being applied at checkout. Can you help?” floating above the hero photo.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3
